symptom: ako/mxcli#1685: `retrieve $Items from Shop.Item where [Total > @Shop.C_Limit];` was a parse error (`mismatched input 'Shop' expecting ']'`), read as 'MDL cannot write a constant in an XPath'. Worse, silent: a page data source written `where Total > @Shop.C_Limit` stored `[Total > ]`; describe of any stored constraint holding a constant on an entity with an enum attribute printed `where Total > @;`; and a long one written in the quoted form was laid out and STORED as `[Total > @]`
cause: No XPath rule for a constant: `@` (AT) was admitted by the negated xpathWord set as a one-word name. ParseXPathConstraint (error listeners off) recovered past the module name and returned ok with IdentifierExpr "@", so every re-render of the parse (enum enrichment, FormatXPathConstraint, check's member walk, which reported an attribute named "@") lost the constant; separately the page-side xpathExprToString had no ConstantRefExpr case and rendered "" for the expression-grammar form
file: mdl/grammar/domains/MDLPage.g4 (xpathConstantRef, AT out of xpathWord), mdl/visitor/visitor_xpath.go (buildXPathConstantRef), mdl/visitor/visitor_page_v3.go (xpathExprToString), mdl/executor/validate_xpath_constants.go (MDL-XPATH03), validate_user_role_tokens.go (walkXPathSlots)
fix: `@Module.Name` is an xpathValueExpr (a value, not a step) and AT is no longer a name word; the visitor builds ast.ConstantRefExpr and the page renderer prints it. check refuses a constant in any XPath slot (MDL-XPATH03, ValidateProgram, no project needed) with the variable workaround; excluded flows warn
test: mdl/visitor/visitor_xpath_constant_test.go, mdl/executor/validate_xpath_constants_test.go, mdl/executor/xpath_constant_1685_test.go (PedApp: stored verbatim in retrieve, list view and access rule, describe -> exec writes nothing, rename constant rewrites all three). Reverting the grammar fails every test with the reported parse error and `[Total > @]`; reverting only the renderer case gives `[Total > ]`
insight: The issue's premise was wrong and only a measurement showed it: mxbuild 11.13.0 rejects `@Mod.C` in a retrieve (Integer, String, Boolean constant), a list view data source, an access rule and a user task's targeting with CE0161, and an UNKNOWN constant is the same CE0161 rather than CE1613 (11.15.0 agrees for the retrieve) - XPath never resolves the name; the variable form is clean. So the right fix for this parse error was to parse it and REFUSE it with the workaround, not to store it. The Mendix runtime's MxPath grammar does have a CONSTANT token (com.mendix.languages.jar), which is why the syntax looks plausible. Access-rule XPaths are not validated by mx check at all while project security is Off - a garbage `[Total >]` passes - so measure access rules under Production security, with a bad-constraint control. A lenient parse that returns ok is not evidence it read everything: grep a renderer for `default: return ""` before trusting a new AST node to round-trip
